**Surah 110: al-Nasr (The Divine Support)**

It is also called *al-Tawdi'* (The Farewell).

Its purpose is to inform of the completion of the religion, which is necessarily implied by the meaning of its name, *al-Nasr* (Divine Support). From this it necessarily follows that the Prophet ﷺ would die. From this it necessarily follows the knowledge that he appeared in the world of existence and corruption only to raise the word of Allah the Exalted and to abolish the word of Satan, upon whom be the curse of Allah the Exalted. From this it necessarily follows that he (ﷺ) is the essence of existence and the greatest servant of the Loving Protector. This is also indicated by its name, *al-Tawdi'*, and by the circumstances of its revelation, which were the days of *al-Tashriq* (the days of sacrifice after the Day of Sacrifice) in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage (*Hijjat al-Wada'*).

**"In the name of Allah"**, to Whom belongs all command. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

**"The Most Merciful"**, who sent you as a mercy to the worlds. After bestowing the gift of existence, He extended His mercy to them by making clear to them, in the utmost clarity, the path of salvation through you, for the sustaining of their livelihood and their final return, through the inimitable Qur'an that was revealed to you. Whoever hears it is as if he heard it from the Most High, the Mighty.

**"The Most Compassionate"**, who singled out whoever He wills to turn toward Him, by admitting him to His party and making him among the people of His nearness, through adherence to the Straight Path.

* *

Since the preceding surah indicated that the unbelievers had reached a state in which they were of no consequence, no regard was to be given to them, and no concern was to be felt about them in any way, so long as the situation was one of disengagement, it was as if it were said: "Will there then be a victory over them and a triumph against them through battle?" This surah answers: as good news for the believers and a warning for the unbelievers. But since this did not actually take place until the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, two years after the conquest of Makkah, it was as though the conquest had not been firmly established until then. Therefore Allah, glorified and exalted, did not reveal this surah except at that time, and before the Prophet's return from the battle of Hunayn. He, Exalted, said, confirming that He supports the oppressed, exalts His religion, gives respite but does not neglect, and that nothing can overpower Him. This encourages reliance upon Him and sufficiency in Him. The object of "*sabbih*" (glorify) is placed first, to hasten the good news: **"When"**.

Since the decreed matters are directed from eternity toward their appointed times, driven toward them by the driver of power, drawing nearer to them little by little, it is as though they are coming toward them. Therefore the figurative use of "coming" for "occurring" arises, and He said: **"has come"**, that is, has become established and fixed in the future by the arrival of its time, which was set in eternity. He increased its magnification by its being attributed to Him, then by its being the Name of the Essence, and so He said: **"the support of Allah"**, that is, the Sovereign, the Greatest, who has no equal and before whom no one has any command over all people, in every matter He intends.

Since support has degrees, and He, glorified, had indicated by the unrestricted attribution [of support] to Him, and then by its attribution to the Greatest Name, that what is meant is its highest degree, He stated it explicitly, saying: **"and the victory"**, that is, the absolute victory, suitable for every conquest, which this surah was revealed about at Hudaybiyyah, giving good news to him of the triumph of his party, whose leader and guide and director you are, especially over Makkah, where His House is and from where His religion appeared, where its origin was, where its pillar was established, and whose armies were mighty. By this, all the Arabs were humbled, and they said: "We have no strength against one whom Allah has granted victory over the people of the Sacred Precinct." Thus they became mighty through this humiliation, until the completion of this conquest occurred among some of them, and the conquest of all lands would come about through them all. To indicate dominion over all nations, He expressed it in the form of a conditional, and to affirm its certainty He expressed it with "*idha*" (when), informing that He does not break His promise and does not diminish what He has decreed, even if minds imagine that its time has passed, and to announce that hearts are in His hand, turning them however He wills, so that the one who knows this may attain sincerity, fear, and hope. The expression thus conveys that the time has drawn near. The meaning is: be watchful for its arrival and prepared to give thanks for it.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When His religion was perfected, His law made clear, and his affair firmly established, and he had discharged the trust of his message in the fullest manner, he ﷺ came to know the exhaustion of his lifespan and the end of his term. As a sign of this, people were made to enter the religion of Allah in groups after hesitation and reluctance: **"Perfect wisdom, but warnings avail not"** (Qur'an 54:5) and **"Had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance"** (Qur'an 6:35).

He commanded him to increase in seeking forgiveness, which is prescribed at the close of gatherings, at the ends of the day, and at the conclusion of undertakings, to make up for whatever idle talk or slackness might intervene. Allah, glorified and exalted, therefore legislated seeking forgiveness, so that He might secure for His servants, through the preservation of their states and the guarding of their times, what would fulfill for them the lofty rewards, as He promised them: **"And the word of your Lord is fulfilled in truth and justice; none can alter His words"** (Qur'an 6:115).

I have expanded upon what this great surah indicates (and all the speech of our Lord is great) in what I have written elsewhere. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, understood from it that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been informed of the nearness of his death before his Lord, and he recognized the imminence of his end. This same purpose was also indicated, more remotely from the actual event, in this surah by the verse: **"This day I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion"** (Qur'an 5:3). And Surah Bara'ah (al-Tawbah) and his actions ﷺ at the Farewell Pilgrimage [also indicated it]. However, we have no report that any of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, perceived the matter specifically except from this surah. It became clearly known through the indication of Surah Bara'ah and the verse of al-Ma'idah. The people sensed it during the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage and at the revelation of Bara'ah, but they did not become certain of it, and their hope for his life prevailed, and some of them died. When **"When the support of Allah and the victory has come"** was revealed, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, became certain of that with a certainty that moved him to weep when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it. End.

And you see the people, that is, the Arabs, who were despised among all the nations, so that through you they became "the people" (as the lam of perfection indicates), and the rest of the people of the earth became their followers, and in relation to them, subjects. They enter, [coming] little by little, their entry being renewed and continuous, into the religion of Allah, that is, the Sharia of the One whose word has never ceased to be supreme, whether the creation refuses it, by His subduing them to the disbelief which no sensible person would wish for himself, leaving their desires aside, or while they are obedient, by His compelling them to obedience. He expressed it by "religion" (din), whose meaning is recompense (jaza'), because the Arabs did not believe in the Resurrection, without which the manifestation of recompense is not complete. ﴿In companies﴾, that is, tribe after tribe, troop after troop, and dense groups, like an entire tribe as one community after another, such as the people of Makkah, al-Ta'if, Hawazin, Hamdan and all the other tribes, [without -] fighting, in ease, speed, suddenness and gentleness, after entering one by one and the like. This is because they said: "If he prevails over the people of the Sacred Precinct, whom Allah protected from the companions of the Elephant, whom no one could repel, then we have no power against them." Thus it becomes clear that this syllogism, which produced this self-evident result, was arranged by Allah only as a preparation (irhas) for His prophethood and a foundation for His call, so they laid down their arms and surrendered their leadership, both the settled and the nomadic among them.

(p-٣١٧) Since the implied meaning is: "He has truly glorified Allah Himself with praise, by actually driving the filth of polytheism from the Arabian Peninsula," He said, as a notice that He is exalted above deficiencies, including the breaking of promises, and that He possesses, together with that, majesty and beauty. He expressed it in a form that conveys wonder, to increase the magnification of the one who is being wondered at, so that this produces reverence, exaltation, humility, and acceptance of all commands. The command of the Exalted to the Prophet ﷺ is understood as concerning [his own self, in that his appointed time is near, and that his concern] with the people has ended, because the religion has been perfected, and so there remains for him ﷺ no preoccupation in this abode of turbidity: ﴿So glorify﴾, meaning: exalt Him, by your words and your deeds, through prayer and other acts, in agreement with your Lord regarding what He has done, and increase in all kinds of worship, glorifying Him while clothed in ﴿praise﴾, meaning: with perfection, honor, and magnification, of ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who fulfilled for you His promise by completing the religion and suppressing the transgressors, who has done good to you in all of that, because all of it is for your honor. Otherwise He is Mighty and Praiseworthy in every state. This is in wonder at how Allah facilitated this conquest, which had not occurred to the mind, and in gratitude for what He, glorified and exalted be He, bestowed upon him [by showing him the completion of that for which he was sent], and because every good deed that his followers perform has a like reward for him.

When He commanded him ﷺ to exalt Him above every deficiency, and described Him, descending (p-٣١٨) from the Hidden of the Hidden to the Hidden, with every perfection attributed to the Lord, bringing Himself down to the witnessing of acts, He reached the limit of descent from the Creator to the created, addressing the highest of all creation, and commanded him with what conveys inability to fulfill His right, because of His greatness indicated by mentioning it twice, by the Greatest Name, which has among its indications of magnitude and loftiness the reaching to the place of the Unseen, which no hope can attain, where necks are cut short before it, so that the inability of others may be understood a fortiori. He said, teaching that it is part of His perfection that He seizes sin if He wills and forgives if He wills, even if the sin is great, so that this may urge hastening to repentance, increasing good deeds, and good hope: ﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾, meaning: ask Him for forgiveness, ﴿indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾, as a notice that no one can estimate Him as He truly deserves. This is as indicated by that seeking forgiveness after prayer, which is the greatest of acts of worship, so that your community may follow you in persisting in the second security for them. For the first security, which is your presence among them, has drawn near to its return to its source in the Highest Companionship and the most holy station of the First. Likewise the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "Glory be to You; I cannot count the praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself." He entered Mecca on the day of the Conquest with his head bowed, to the point that it nearly touched the saddle's center, in humility before Allah, glorified and exalted be He, informing his companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, that what occurred (p-٣١٩) was only by the power of Allah, not by the multitude of those with him. He made them a means out of His kindness toward them. For this reason, He admonished whoever among them thought, or whose mind suggested, that numbers had a role in what happened, both in the defeat at Hunayn first, and in what followed of victory through those who remained with the Prophet ﷺ, who numbered fewer than thirty souls, second. Thus the glorification, which is exaltation above deficiency, is an indication of His completing the religion, in fulfillment of what His noble promise had previously stated.

And the seeking of forgiveness is an indication that the worship of his ﷺ, which is the greatest worship, has come close to its end, and this can only be by death. Therefore he was commanded to seek forgiveness, because it occurs at the conclusion of gatherings and deeds, [as a compensation] for whatever shortcoming may have occurred in them, with a kind of weakness, and as acknowledgment of the pure servanthood and inability.

When he was commanded with that, the context guided to the implied meaning: "And turn to Him in repentance." He gave the reason for it, emphasizing it in order to refute one who finds the content of this improbable, namely the return of people to apostasy and others, with His saying: ﴿Indeed He﴾, meaning: the One who does you the utmost good by His making you successor in your community. It is also possible that the emphasis is for the sake of the indication that what preceded, the mention of the Majestic Name twice, points to the utmost greatness and the escape from comprehension (p-٣٢٠) by His veiling through His will, the pride, the might, the tyranny, and the subjugation, although it is customary that whoever has some of these qualities is such that he accepts no excuse and accepts no penitent. ﴿Was﴾, meaning: He has never ceased to be, in renewal and continuity, ﴿Accepting of repentance﴾, meaning: One who returns, toward whomever He refined the devil through, from the people of His mercy. He is the One who turned your helpers back from what they were upon of gathering in disbelief, discord, and enmity, and so He strengthened you by their entering the religion little by little, until they hastened in great numbers after the Chapter of the Conquest, until they entered Mecca, ten thousand strong. He also brings you back to the state through which the manifestation of your elevation in the Highest Companionship increases, and He returns the slackening of your community in its religion, by apostasy or disobedience short of that, to what it was of goodness, and He leads them in the best course. Thus the end of the surah has returned to its beginning, for had the description of Him as Accepting of repentance not been realized, He would not have provided the helper through whom the conquest was achieved. The ending of it joins the beginning of it, and it is known that each sentence in it is caused by what precedes it. So Allah's acceptance of repentance toward His servant is the result of his repentance by his seeking forgiveness, which [is] the request for forgiveness with its conditions, and that is the fruit of his belief in the perfection of his Lord. This is what is indicated by His exalting His religion, and His compelling those who enter it to enter, although [they were] among the people most unyielding and highest in resolve and determination, and they had been in the utmost refusal toward it and in contending against its bearer. That is the benefit of the Conquest, and it is the sign of victory. It is known that the last verse is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two corresponding elements are each mentioned in one place and omitted in the other). It indicates the command to repentance by the command to seek forgiveness, and the reason for the command to repentance indicates the reason for the command to seek forgiveness. It is known that the surah is an indication of his ﷺ death, through the urging to seek forgiveness, which is the second security, and it is proper that deeds and gatherings be concluded with it, after what its announcement indicated by the victory of the religion over all religions, and its descent in the middle of the days of Tashriq (p-٣٢١) of his pilgrimage, upon him be the best prayers and peace, in the year ten, as I mentioned in my book "Masa'id al-Nazar li'l-Ishraf 'ala Maqasid al-Suwar" and my book "al-Ittila' 'ala Hajjat al-Wada'," and that was after the descent of the verse of al-Ma'idah, which is its counterpart in returning the end to the beginning, on the day of 'Arafah:

﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3]. It is well known that there is no perfection in this abode except that after it there is deficiency. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ named it the Farewell Pilgrimage, and he addressed the people in it, teaching them the matters of their religion, and had them testify against themselves, and called Allah to witness against them (p-٣٢٢) that he had conveyed to them. He bade them farewell and said: "I do not know, perhaps I will not meet you after this year of mine." He also indicated by the repentance, and by the occurrence of apostasy after him ﷺ, and the return of those who apostatized to the best of what they had been upon in their belief in the religion and their steadfastness in it, by killing those who were stamped with disbelief, indicated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And had He made them hear﴾ [al-Anfal: 23], meaning: hearing of subjugation, domination, and compulsion, ﴿they would have turned away while they were averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. So their existence was pure harm without any benefit, and their killing was benefit with no harm in it in any way. And for the sake of understanding it, the approach of the appointed time is for the announcement of completion. "Al-'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him" — and in another narration: his son 'Abdullah — wept when it was revealed, and the Prophet ﷺ asked him, and he said: "You have been informed of your own death," and he said: "Indeed it is as you say." Just as 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, wept at the descent of the verse of al-Ma'idah, and he gave this as the reason. And Allah is the Guide. It has become clear from this that its essential purpose is the announcement of the perfection of the religion and the nearness of the death of the Seal of the Prophets, and victory over all the oppressors, tyrants, and transgressors. That is among the greatest aims of al-Ma'idah, which is parallel to this in the correspondence between the beginning and the end, as indicated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], (p-٣٢٣) the verse, and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies, indeed the party of Allah are the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 56], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 120]. Among the greatest subtleties of this surah and the finest of its wonders and most delicate of its aims is that its words, by their counts, indicate great matters and beautiful secrets. Its words number nineteen. In the year nineteen after the Hijrah, the death of Caesar, tyrant of the Romans, occurred. When 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, conquered Alexandria, Caesar said: "If they overcome us at Alexandria, the Romans are ruined," so he prepared himself to fight them personally. When he finished his preparations, Allah struck him down and he died, and Allah spared the Muslims his evil, and the Romans were humiliated by that with great humiliation, and the Arabs became bold. In this same year also, Allah conquered Caesarea of the lands of al-Sham, and no enemy remained in al-Sham, far or near. The Muslims rejoiced at that with intense joy. In it also was the conquest of Jalula', of the lands of Persia, and its conquest was called the Conquest of Conquests, because the Persians were not restored after it. This is if we count what corresponds to its words from the year of the Hijrah. If we count from the year of the descent of the surah, which was the year ten, then Istakhr was conquered in the twenty-ninth year of the Hijrah, which is the nineteenth year from its descent, (p-٣٢٤) the city of Istakhr, and the weakness of the Persians became severe, and their king Yazdegerd's command and his efforts in fleeing from the Arabs continued until he was killed in the thirty-first year of the Hijrah, two years after that. That is the count corresponding to the count of its words, outwardly and inwardly, together with the words of the basmalah. If you look at what is here in this regard and compare it with what was mentioned in the surah of al-Fath of its like, your wonder at the dazzling of these verses will increase. And Allah is the Granter of success. Then, if you consider another consideration, you will find that this surah, just as it indicates by its totality the end of the period of prophethood with the death of the Prophet ﷺ, it indicates by the individual words of its statements the end of the caliphate of prophethood after a complete thirty years, as the Prophet ﷺ said, as narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, from Safinah, the freedman of the Prophet ﷺ, and may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 110, verse 3 (part 2 of 2):

"The caliphate of prophethood lasts thirty years, then [God] gives kingship to whom He wills." This is because, if you count its words together with the basmala (the formula "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate"), they number twenty-three words by the rasm (the written orthography). This points to the end of the caliphate, which was never a caliphate like it, namely the caliphate of al-Faruq 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, through his martyrdom in Dhu al-Hijjah in the year twenty-three of the Hijra. If you add to that the explicit pronouns, which are five, and the implicit pronouns, which are three, the total is thirty-one. [p. 325] I have calculated that from the time the surah was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ in Dhu al-Hijjah of the year ten, this points to the end of the entire caliphate of prophethood with the reconciliation of Amir al-Mu'minin al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may God be pleased with them both, in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal of the year forty-one. That was exactly thirty years after the death of the Prophet ﷺ in Rabi' al-Awwal of the year ten of the Hijra, not a month more or less.

If the pronouns alone, explicit and implicit, are taken, they point precisely to the conquest of the honoured Makkah. For they are, as has passed, eight, and the conquest took place in the year eight of the Hijra. Among the subtle secrets and wondrous insights is that they indicate the years according to the detail: the explicit [pronoun] indicates the year of victory and dominance over Quraysh, because they are the primary intended ones, since the Arabs follow them. The implicit [pronoun] indicates the opposite of that. The explanation of this is that when, in the first year of the Hijra, the banners of Islam had fluttered in every direction, and its lions had spread in every region, and its expeditions had scattered throughout every land, the ta' in ﴿ورأيت﴾ [al-Nasr: 2], which is his pronoun ﷺ, pointed to that, as an allusion to what is specific to his understanding of the good news. When, in the second year, the Battle of Badr brought such clear success and great victory that it broke the hearts of the unbelievers and strengthened the hearts of the Ansar in all the regions, and raised their rank, the waw in ﴿يدخلون﴾ [al-Nasr: 2] pointed to that. When, in the third year, there occurred the calamity, which was not feared, at the Battle of Uhud, which perhaps led some who had not firmly established themselves to think of a defect, the implicit pronoun in ﴿فسبح﴾ pointed to that. When, in the fourth year, there came news of the expulsion of Bani al-Nadir and of Quraysh breaking their promise from Badr, out of cowardice and incapacity, whereas the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, may God the Exalted be pleased with them, showed courage and strength by the power of God, and they returned "with a blessing from God and grace; no harm touched them" [Al 'Imran: 174], the kaf in ﴿ربك﴾ pointed to that. When, in the fifth year, there was the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), the implicit [pronoun] pointed to it in ﴿واستغفره﴾. When, in the sixth year, there was the 'Umrah of al-Hudaybiyah, which the Prophet ﷺ called a victory, God sent down in it Surat al-Fath, [because it was the cause of the conquest, and that was one of the signs of prophethood, and because the Prophet ﷺ sent in it to the kings calling them to God the Exalted] pointed to that, the explicit pronoun in ﴿واستغفره﴾, and confirmed its strength by [its being] for the Lord the Exalted. When, in the seventh year, there were the Battle of Khaybar and the 'Umrat al-Qada', the explicit pronoun in ﴿إنه﴾ pointed to them. And when the pronoun of [﴿كان﴾ refers to God, and for Him, glory be to Him, there are two presences: the presence of the unseen and the hidden, and the presence of witnessing and manifestation, and the presence of the unseen was] the presence of majesty, grandeur, greatness and exaltation, while the presence of witnessing is the presence of descent through actions and of seeking favour through words, both presences were for victory, and the presence of the unseen was the greater of the two in victory and the stronger in support. Therefore the implicit pronoun indicated the greatest conquest, through victory over the inhabitants and the abodes, by the might of the One, the Subduer. Moreover, if we look at it from the standpoint of its being capable of being manifest, the manifest [pronoun] has its ruling. Glory be to Him whose knowledge encompasses all, whose wisdom is subtle, and whose decree is executed.
